findings.title: Default, namespace and unknown imports from "bun:bundle" are dropped silently and leave undeclared bindings.
findings.body: Only named items are checked. For `import * as b from "bun:bundle"` or `import f from "bun:bundle"`, the statement is removed with no diagnostic and no symbol is declared. `b.feature("X")` then builds without error and fails at runtime with a ReferenceError. Unknown named specifiers get a warning that says they "will be undefined", but they are never declared either, so using them also throws a ReferenceError rather than giving `undefined`. Report an error for default and namespace imports. For unknown specifiers, either declare them or raise an error. The same problem applies to a non-call use of `feature`, such as `const f = feature`, which is left pointing at a binding that no longer exists.

findings.title: Pointer to an embedded `config.features` field can be passed to `allocator.destroy` in `BundleOptions.deinit`.
findings.body: `BundleOptions.deinit` now calls `.deinit()` and `allocator.destroy()` on any `bundler_feature_flags` pointer that is not the static empty set. Here the pointer is set to `&config.features`, a field inside the JS bundler config. That config is not a separate heap allocation, and `Config.deinit` already frees it (`self.features.deinit()`). If this transpiler's `deinit` runs, the result is a double free and an invalid `destroy` of a non-heap pointer. Even if it does not run, the transpiler holds a pointer into a config that may be freed first. Track ownership with a flag, or clone the set into a heap allocation that the transpiler owns. I could not see whether this bundle-thread transpiler is ever deinit'd.

findings.title: Feature flags are not part of the runtime transpiler cache key.
findings.body: `bundler_feature_flags` changes the transpiled output, but it is not added to `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler`, and nothing else in the change hashes the set's contents. `bun run` and `bun test` can reuse cached output from the runtime transpiler cache, which applies to larger files. So if you run `bun run --feature=X big.ts` and then `bun run big.ts`, the second run can get the cached output with `feature("X")` already folded to `true`, or the other way round. The fix is to mix a hash of the sorted flag names into the cache key, or to turn the cache off whenever any `bun:bundle` feature call is replaced.

held.title: The feature-flag set has no clear owner, so copies of the options can double free it or leak it.
held.body: `BundleOptions` is copied by value in several places, for example when worker or child transpilers are created from a parent. Each copy keeps the same `bundler_feature_flags` pointer, and each copy's `deinit` would free and destroy it again. Separately, `build_command.zig` line 85 replaces a set that `fromApi` already allocated from the same `ctx.args.feature_flags`, so the first set leaks. Give one owner the job of freeing the set (an ownership flag works), and reuse the set that already exists instead of allocating it twice.

held.title: The flag lookup ignores rope (concatenated) e_string values.
held.body: `flag_string.data` holds only the first segment when an `E.String` is a rope, for example after constant folding of `"FOO" + "BAR"`. The lookup would then test `FOO` instead of `FOOBAR` and return the wrong value. Reject ropes (`next != null`) or resolve them to the full string before calling `contains`.
